title: Identifying key genes for European canker resistance in apple: machine learning and gene expression profiling of quantitative disease resistance.
summary: Twenty-six stable transcriptional predictors; 4CL/phenylpropanoid, NLR/RLK/WAK and epigenetic-regulator transcripts associated with partial resistance across six QTLs. Genotype-blocked five-fold CV on 20 full-sibling genotypes; separate expression validation in ‘Golden Delicious’ and ‘M9 EMLA’. Accuracy was 0.67 in CV and 1.00 in the two-cultivar validation table, whose small cultivar sample and limited generalizability are explicit caveats.
ai_technology: Random Forest variable-importance selection with genotype-blocked stability selection identified resistance-predictive transcripts from RNA-seq; expression/QTL analyses then localized candidate genes and pathways.

source_review.scope: The primary Research Square v1 (posted 2025-12-01) and the linked Scientific Reports article describe the same result: genotype-blocked Random Forest feature selection ranked 26 stable transcripts for European canker resistance; the model reached 0.67 accuracy in genotype-blocked five-fold testing (95% CI 0.55–0.77, p=0.021), and expression patterns were checked in a separate ‘Golden Delicious’/‘M9 EMLA’ dataset. The paper links candidate defense, phenylpropanoid and regulatory genes to six resistance QTLs. The independent check covers two cultivars and the authors state broader cultivar and functional validation is still needed; this is a candidate-marker result, not proof of causal resistance genes. No matching DOI or same-result record appears in the active or archived catalog; prior QTL mapping is a different result.
